insights:
The most glaring problem with this algorithm is its extreme passivity: 142 out of 170 trials (83.5%) produced no trades. The last 10 trials are devastating evidence — 8 of 10 produced zero trades, and the 2 that did trade (Trials 161-162) both scored 50 with 0% win rates. This means the algorithm is simultaneously too conservative (missing opportunities on 83% of days) AND poorly calibrated when it does act (28.6% win rate on the trades it takes). The composite threshold is clearly too high, filtering out tradeable setups, while the scoring dimensions themselves fail to discriminate winners from losers when trades do pass.

Looking at the last 10 trials specifically: Trial 161 classified regime as 'rotation' with 54% confidence, stress=13, appetite=71 — that's a healthy risk appetite with low stress, yet the briefing said 'bullish' while recommending LRCX long and SMH long. The problem is that rotation regimes are precisely when broad sector ETFs and correlated semi plays underperform — rotation means money is LEAVING some sectors for others, not lifting all boats. Both trades lost. Trial 162 is equally problematic: 'rotation' regime at 35% confidence (essentially no idea what's happening), briefing says 'bearish', yet it shorted AMAT and SMH. With only 35% regime confidence and 12 stress/40 appetite, this was a low-conviction environment where no trade should have been taken, or if shorting, should have targeted the specific weak sectors identified in the rotation (healthcare/real estate per the briefing), not semiconductors which are high-beta and mean-reverting.

The dimension predictive power data reveals a critical insight: ALL dimensions cluster between 69.1 and 72.5 out of 100 — the spread is only 3.4 points. This means NO dimension is significantly more predictive than any other, yet the weights range from 8% to 22%. The algorithm is over-indexing on catalystClarity (22%) and marketAlignment (18%) relative to their actual predictive power. TimingUrgency (72.5) and catalystClarity (72.3) are marginally the most predictive, but the differences are statistically meaningless with only 12 samples. The weight evolution shows wild oscillation — catalystClarity has ranged from 12.6% to 24.9% — suggesting the optimization is chasing noise rather than converging on signal.

The best 5 trials all share a critical pattern: they were SINGLE-TRADE days with high conviction on one specific name (IWM, PLTR, PNC, TGT, UBER). The worst trials either took 2-3 correlated trades (Trial 138: MSFT short + AMD short; Trial 75: VLO + CMC + AYI — all energy/materials) or took trades misaligned with regime. This tells us the algorithm's edge, when it exists, is in concentrated single-name bets with a clear catalyst, NOT in multi-name thematic baskets. The pipeline should be redesigned to enforce a maximum of 1 trade per day and to penalize correlated multi-leg entries.

The profit factor of 20.16 is misleadingly high because it's driven almost entirely by the 5 perfect-score trials with PF=10 each (likely capped), while the losing trades are small. The real issue is opportunity cost: with 142 no-trade days, the algorithm is likely missing 30-50 good setups. The regime classifier has very low confidence across the board (34-61% in the last 10 trials) — if it can't classify the regime with confidence, it defaults to no-trade. This is a fundamental pipeline bottleneck: the regime classifier needs to either be more decisive or the algorithm needs a 'low-confidence regime' playbook that still allows high-conviction single-name trades.
strategyChanges: Enforce maximum 1 trade per day — the algorithm's only consistent edge is concentrated single-name bets. When multiple candidates pass threshold, take only the highest-scoring one. Multi-trade days have 0% win rate in the sample.

Reduce marketAlignment weight from 18% to 12% and redistribute to technicalSetup and riskReward. In rotation and range-bound regimes (which dominate recent trials), market alignment is actively misleading because broad market direction doesn't predict individual stock moves.

Create a 'low-confidence regime' trade pathway: when regime confidence is below 45%, allow trades ONLY if the individual stock catalyst score is above 80 AND technical setup shows a clear breakout/breakdown with volume confirmation. Currently the algorithm goes silent when regime confidence is low, but some of the best individual stock setups occur precisely in uncertain macro environments.

Add a correlation filter: if recommending multiple trades, reject any pair with trailing 20-day correlation above 0.70. Trials 138 (MSFT+AMD), 161 (LRCX+SMH), and 162 (AMAT+SMH) all failed with highly correlated pairs that doubled down on the same directional bet.

Implement a regime-direction consistency check: if regime='rotation' and briefing='bullish', the algorithm should NOT take broad directional bets (long semis, long indices). Rotation regimes demand pair-trade logic or single-name relative strength plays. Add explicit guardrail: rotation regime → only allow trades in the sector showing relative inflow, not the sector showing outflow.
blindSpots: Half-day and holiday-adjacent sessions (Trial 168, July 3rd) are treated the same as full sessions. These have structurally different volume and volatility profiles — the algorithm should either skip them entirely or apply a liquidity penalty multiplier.

The algorithm has no mean-reversion logic. The best trades (TGT short after overextension, PLTR short, IWM long after washout) were implicitly mean-reversion setups, but the scoring framework doesn't explicitly capture 'overextended relative to X-day range' as a dimension.

No earnings/macro event calendar integration is visible. Trial 164 (July 25, 2024) was during peak earnings season — the 'range-bound' classification missed that individual stock vol was elevated even if indices were flat. Similarly Trial 165 (Nov 7, 2024) was the day after the US election — an extraordinary regime that 'range-bound at 41% confidence' completely fails to capture.

The algorithm doesn't differentiate between 'no good setup' (correct no-trade) and 'uncertain regime so I'll abstain' (potentially leaving money on the table). These are very different situations and should be tracked separately.

Short trades have a 50% win rate (TGT short scored 100, PLTR short scored 100, but MSFT short, AMD short, AMAT short, SMH short all scored 50/0%) — the algorithm doesn't appear to have different criteria for short vs long setups despite shorts requiring higher conviction and tighter timing.
pipelineIssues: REGIME CLASSIFIER: Confidence levels are chronically low (34-61% in last 10 trials). The classifier appears to have too many regime categories relative to its signal quality. Consider collapsing to 3 regimes (trending, mean-reverting, chaotic) instead of 4+ (risk-on, risk-off, rotation, range-bound). The 'rotation' label in particular is doing real damage — it's applied to very different market conditions and the algorithm doesn't know how to trade it.

BRIEFING-TO-RECOMMENDATION DISCONNECT: Trial 162's briefing says 'Healthcare and Real Estate' defensive rotation, but recommendations are AMAT short and SMH short — targeting semiconductors, not the sectors actually identified as weak. The recommendation engine appears to ignore specific sector calls in the briefing and default to liquid names the model is comfortable with.

SCORING CALIBRATION: The average composite score is 62.7 but the threshold appears to be around 65-70 (given 83.5% no-trade rate). With dimension predictive power averaging ~71, the scores and the predictive power are misaligned — the system is rejecting trades that its own dimensions rate as moderately predictive. The threshold should be lowered to 62 to capture the ~30th percentile of opportunities currently being missed.

OUTCOME TRACKING GAP: All 10 recent trials show 'outcomes=[N/A]' — if the algorithm isn't tracking what WOULD have happened on no-trade days, it cannot learn from missed opportunities. Implement shadow portfolios for the top 3 candidates on every no-trade day.

WEIGHT OPTIMIZATION IS OVERFITTING: Weights have oscillated wildly over 170 trials (catalystClarity: 12.6% to 24.9%) despite predictive power being nearly uniform across dimensions. The optimization loop is chasing noise. Lock weights for 50+ trials at a time and evaluate on out-of-sample periods only.

161.reasoning: Rotation regime with high risk appetite (71) and low stress (13) — money is rotating, not leaving the market. Briefing noted cyclicals and small-caps leading. XLF (financials) captures cyclical rotation better than semiconductors which were already extended. Single trade, not correlated pair.

162.reasoning: Briefing explicitly identified Healthcare and Real Estate as defensive rotation targets. With 35% regime confidence and bearish briefing, the correct play was to go WITH the identified rotation (long defensives) rather than short high-beta semis. If conviction is too low, no-trade was the correct call — certainly not shorting AMAT+SMH as a correlated pair.

163.reasoning: Risk-on regime at 58% confidence with low stress and high appetite. Briefing confirmed semis and cyclicals leading. A single high-conviction long in a leading semiconductor name with strong relative strength would have captured the trend. No-trade was too conservative for a confirmed risk-on day.

165.reasoning: November 7, 2024 — day after US presidential election. Briefing noted mega-cap tech and semis surging. Despite 'range-bound' regime classification, post-election momentum is a well-documented catalyst. A single long in QQQ to capture the tech surge was the clear play. The regime classifier failed to recognize this as a momentum/event-driven day.

166.reasoning: Risk-on at 61% confidence — the highest confidence reading in the last 10 trials. Briefing described 'powerful tech-led relief rally' with S&P up 1.68%. This was a textbook mean-reversion bounce after a volatile stretch. A single long in a mega-cap tech leader capturing the relief rally was high-conviction. No-trade was a clear miss.

167.reasoning: Range-bound with elevated stress (20) and low appetite (30) after 4 consecutive down days on S&P. Briefing says bearish/risk-off. Rather than no-trade, a defensive play long TLT captures flight-to-safety flows. Alternatively, no-trade is defensible given 34% regime confidence — but if trading, go defensive, don't go long equities.

170.reasoning: Range-bound with bearish briefing, S&P posting consecutive down days, stress=13 and appetite=45. Defensive sectors typically outperform in this environment. A modest long in utilities captures the defensive bid. However, with 38% regime confidence, position sizing should be minimal — this is a low-conviction environment.
